project_type: Cost-minimized fully-serverless AWS quiz application. Backend = AWS CDK v2 (TypeScript): API Gateway v2 HTTP API -> ARM64 Node.js 22 Lambda -> DynamoDB single-table (on-demand), plus Cognito User Pool + Hosted UI for admin auth. Frontend is being REBUILT from a dependency-free vanilla-JS SPA into a modern React + Vite + TypeScript SPA (user chose Option B). Amplify Hosting serves the frontend.
language: TypeScript. New frontend = React 18 + Vite 5 + TypeScript 5. Backend/CDK/Lambda unchanged (TypeScript).
build_system: TWO separate npm projects. (1) Root package.json = CDK project (aws-cdk-lib, jest, tsc) - DO NOT TOUCH except leave as-is. (2) NEW frontend/package.json = the Vite React app with its own node_modules, scripts: dev/build/preview. Vite build output goes to frontend/dist. Env vars exposed to the client MUST be prefixed VITE_ and read via import.meta.env. Amplify build runs `npm ci && npm run build` inside frontend/.
test_framework: Backend: jest + ts-jest (test/*.test.ts) - unchanged, keep passing. Frontend: no test runner is being added (keep dependency count lean); verification is `tsc --noEmit` (via `vite build` which type-checks through tsc -b) and `vite build` succeeding. Do NOT add jest/vitest to the frontend unless trivially free.
build_command: Backend (root, on networked machine): `env -u NODE_OPTIONS npm ci && npm run build`. Frontend (in frontend/, on networked machine): `env -u NODE_OPTIONS npm install && env -u NODE_OPTIONS npm run build`.
test_command: Backend (root): `env -u NODE_OPTIONS npm test`. Frontend: `env -u NODE_OPTIONS npm run build` (type-check + bundle is the gate; no unit tests added).
verification_instructions: IN-SANDBOX (INTEGRATIONS_ONLY, npm registry 403): cannot npm install / vite build / tsc. Verify by: JSON validity of package.json/tsconfig; reading TS/TSX for correctness-by-construction; confirming import paths resolve against declared deps; confirming env-var wiring (VITE_* names match amplify.yml); confirming API request/response shapes match lambda/index.ts exactly. ON NETWORKED MACHINE (user, EC2): `cd frontend && env -u NODE_OPTIONS npm install && env -u NODE_OPTIONS npm run build` must succeed and produce frontend/dist; backend `env -u NODE_OPTIONS npm ci && npm run build && npm test` must still pass. The `env -u NODE_OPTIONS` prefix is a sandbox workaround; the user's real machine may not need it.
snapshot_or_generated_files: No frontend lockfile is committed (do NOT fabricate one; user's npm install generates package-lock.json). Vite output frontend/dist is generated at build time and must be gitignored. frontend/node_modules must be gitignored. Backend tsc output (bin/lib/lambda *.js/*.d.ts) and cdk.out already gitignored.
setup_instructions: Frontend local dev: `cd frontend && npm install && npm run dev` (Vite dev server, default http://localhost:5173). Provide env via a local frontend/.env or frontend/.env.local with VITE_API_BASE / VITE_COGNITO_DOMAIN / VITE_COGNITO_CLIENT_ID. Backend deploy unchanged (see README).
environment_constraints: INTEGRATIONS_ONLY network in-sandbox: public npm registry returns 403, so npm install / npm create vite / tsc / vite build CANNOT run here. All frontend files must be authored BY HAND, correct-by-construction, verified by reading. Pick mutually-compatible pinned-ish versions: react 18.3.x, react-dom 18.3.x, react-router-dom 6.x, vite 5.4.x, @vitejs/plugin-react 4.x, typescript ~5.5.x, @types/react 18.3.x, @types/react-dom 18.3.x, @types/node 22.x. No Docker daemon. Do NOT attempt real npm installs, builds, or AWS deploys.
contribution_requirements: Commit onto existing branch feat/cdk-scaffold (do NOT create a new branch, do NOT push - orchestrator publishes, updating PR #1). Preserve ALL existing functionality and the EXACT API contract + Cognito auth model (do NOT change backend/CDK/Lambda, API routes, response shapes, or the Authorization: Bearer <id_token> scheme). Keep cost-minimal spirit: lean deps, Amplify build stays fast; no new backend/idle-cost resources.
key_patterns:
API contract (from lambda/index.ts, MUST match exactly):
- GET {API_BASE}/quizzes -> { quizzes: [{quizId, title, questionCount}] }
- GET {API_BASE}/quizzes/{quizId} -> { quizId, title, questions: [{n, text, options}] } (answerIndex stripped)
- POST {API_BASE}/quizzes/{quizId}/submit  body { answers: number[] } (index = question.n; -1 for unanswered) -> { quizId, score, total, results: [{n, correct, answerIndex}] } (submit DOES return answerIndex, so the result screen can show the correct option)
- POST {API_BASE}/admin/quizzes  body { title, questions:[{text, options, answerIndex}], quizId? }  header Authorization: Bearer <id_token> -> 201 { quizId, title, questionCount }; 400 { message }; 401 (re-login); 403; 409 (already exists)
API_BASE: strip trailing slash; if empty default to '/api'. fetchJson must check res.ok and guard content-type includes application/json (defensive, cross-origin).
Admin quiz-build validation rules to MIRROR exactly: title required (trim); >=1 question; each question text required; collect only NON-EMPTY option strings; require >=2 non-empty options; a correct radio must be selected; answerIndex is computed over the NON-EMPTY options only (skip blanks when counting); optional quizId must match /^[a-z0-9-]+$/. Each question allows 2-4 option rows in the UI; min 2 rows enforced.
Cognito Hosted UI (implicit grant), MIRROR exactly: login URL = {COGNITO_DOMAIN}/login?client_id=...&response_type=token&scope=openid+email+profile&redirect_uri=<adminPageUrl>; capture id_token + expires_in from URL hash, store in sessionStorage under key 'quizAdminToken' as {idToken, expiresAt} with a 60s expiry margin (default 3600s if missing); strip the hash from the URL after capture (history.replaceState); logout URL = {COGNITO_DOMAIN}/logout?client_id=...&logout_uri=<adminPageUrl>; on 401 clear token + prompt re-login; on 403 show 'permission denied'. redirect_uri/logout_uri must equal the admin page's own URL (origin+pathname). NOTE: Cognito callback/logout URLs are configured in CDK to the admin page URL; if using a client-side router the admin route URL must be registered there (documented as a follow-up for the user; keeping /admin.html-equivalent path minimizes churn).
